It catches `ValueError`, `UnitsError`, and `TypeError`, and returns `False` when any of these exceptions occur.

The `UnrecognizedUnit.__eq__` method doesn't wrap the `Unit(other, parse_strict='silent')` call in a try-except block, so when `other` is `None`, the `TypeError` propagates up.

The fix is simple: wrap the `Unit(other, parse_strict='silent')` call in a try-except block similar to what `UnitBase.__eq__` does, or add a check for `None` at the beginning.
